system.summary: Initial-letter code: each group is the initial of a word or syllable with a number (c170 che, i100 il, p149 per); numbering within a letter not alphabetical; z-groups nulls or punctuation. The 'Aditione nel zifra' bound with no. 20 (fr. 3022 f. 50) is of the same design but belongs to another code: only 1 of its 113 groups occurs in these letters.

diacritics.note: the number is written above the base letter

system.sibling_key: No. 20 shares its code with Ranzo's signed letters in fr. 2988 and fr. 3019 no. 27; no contemporary key found. Keys rebuilt by Rosson (6 Oct 2026) and George Lasry (6 Oct 2026).
system.notes: numbering tested not alphabetical (n20/alphatest.py, z = -0.5 vs +6.5 on an alphabetical control), hence key_order random for no. 20. z-groups behave as nulls or punctuation. Split 14 Oct 2026 from targets/vasto1527 (del Vasto's letters are in different ciphers).

prior_solution.where: Rosson (with Claude) 6 Oct 2026, centurione-1528 page: a key for Ranzo's code (no. 20 and fr. 2988 ff. 9-10), built on this project's transcription, found 14 Oct 2026 by a Cryptoole alert, after this project had closed no. 20 as unread. George Lasry reports independent contemporaneous recovery with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, based on Norbert Biermann's transcription (contributed 14 Oct 2026). Cryptiana ranzo.htm (6 Oct 2026) records both. Lasry, 16 Oct 2026, by email to Daniel Bourdeau: 'the Ranzo ciphers are solved Fr 2988 and Fr 20506 - my key or Rosson's key'.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: word-substitution annealer with Kneser-Ney word-bigram Italian LM (n20/solve2.py)
annealers assuming alphabetical order (n20/solve.py, anchor.py, free.py)

solution.what: Fetched fr. 3022 (Gallica btv1b90601558) and identified the three catalogue pieces and folios.
Found no. 10 already solved by Lasry (2023) with Tomokiyo's edited text (2026), and Lasry's 2026 preliminary decryption of Cipher 2 covering no. 6 and no. 19.
Transcribed no. 20 (1,315 groups) and ~2,600 groups of Ranzo's signed letters in fr. 2988; addition sheet transcribed (additione.json).
No. 20 code is initial letter + number, the number running in alphabetical order within each letter (solve.py, anchor.py).
Word annealer (solve2.py) on a held-out 3,900-word Castiglione control encoded the same way: ~46 % token, ~9 % type accuracy.
solve2.py on no. 20 + Ranzo: a stable function-word skeleton (che, il, per, non …) across six restarts; no content words.

Sought cribs: Clair. 327 and Clair. 314 copies (undeciphered), fr. 2988 other cipher pieces (a different French cipher), fr. 3019 no. 27 Ranzo letter (no decipherment), no duplicate text between no. 20 and Ranzo letters.
DECODE R1894 (catalogue 170) identified as the fr. 2988 Ranzo letter already transcribed; no key or decipherment on the record.

Contributed research history: George Lasry, collaborating with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, reconstructed a working Ranzo key from Norbert Biermann’s five-letter transcription. Selected values were checked against the historical addition. The Codex consolidation retains tentative proposals; this is dated source history, not work newly done on 14 October.

A Cryptoole alert (IT1520-1, solved 6 Oct 2026 by Paolo Rosson and George Lasry) led to Rosson's page and files (key/table.tsv, reading/islands.md, decode.py). Their reading uses this project's transcription for fr. 3022 no. 20 and fr. 2988, and a new transcription of the duplicate fr. 3019 ff. 73-74. No. 20 was not unread for lack of a key after all.

Applied Rosson's 779-value key (with his transcription corrections) to n20/f44r-f46v and ranzo_c006-c020. Groups with a value (sure, probable, null): no. 20 93.8%, R1894 (c017-c020) 97.2%; in runs of six or more sure/probable values: no. 20 79.8%, R1894 93.1%. Spot check: c017 and c020 decode as coherent 1528 Italian. Below the 95% bar on the connected-stretch measure; 84 groups of 3,903 have no value. Did not rerun their blind controls.

Prepared the Codex consolidation for contribution: reproduced 541 line-aligned readings, 6,428 cipher occurrences, all 871 key frequencies and two precisely bounded excerpts with translations. Checked the Cryptiana contemporaneous reports. Coverage includes hypotheses and is not measured plaintext correctness.

Split the combined catalogue item 7 target after George Lasry pointed out that it mixed different ciphers: del Vasto's no. 6 (Cipher 2, shifted letters with code groups; sibling no. 19) stays in vasto1527; no. 20 and the Ranzo letters (initial-letter code with numbered word lists) moved to ranzo1528; no. 10 (Cipher 1, read by Lasry and Tomokiyo, not reworked) is a cross-reference only. This folder takes no. 20, the Ranzo transcriptions, Rosson's measure and Lasry's contributed edition.

Tested George Lasry's correction that the addition sheet (fr. 3022 f. 50, additione.json) is not this code's key: of its 113 groups only g217 occurs (once) in the 3,912 transcribed groups of no. 20 and Ranzo's letters, and its numbers overlap the letters' own (b from 157 vs b up to 215 in the letters). The 18 Sept claim that it continues the base lists is withdrawn; page and NOTES corrected.

profile.documents extended to the five letters of George Lasry's package (fr. 2988 f. 2, fr. 2988 ff. 9-10 = R1894, fr. 3022 no. 20, fr. 4050 ff. 79-81, fr. 6638 pp. 67-70), counts from his counts.json; fr. 4050 and fr. 6638 not seen here.

George Lasry, by email: 'the Ranzo ciphers are solved Fr 2988 and Fr 20506 - my key or Rosson's key.' Fr. 20506 ff. 136-138 is the parallel copy of his letter 2 (fr. 2988 ff. 9-10, R1894; DECODE R4450), not a separately transcribed text.

measure_lasry.py: Rosson's key (with his g>214=s, t>196=r rule) applied to Lasry's Biermann transcription and compared token by token with Lasry's key. Where both value a token they agree on 94.4-96.3% per letter (spelling variants such as lettere/littere counted as agreement), including letters 4 and 5, which Rosson never saw. Bar measure per letter: fr. 2988 f. 2 96.2%, ff. 9-10 97.0% (read, with the copy fr. 20506), no. 20 94.4%, fr. 4050 87.7%, fr. 6638 89.0% (read in part); 5,974 of 6,428 overall (92.9%).

Outcome method changed from 'read from existing decipherment' to 'key recovered from ciphertext-only': Lasry's key was rebuilt from the ciphertext with cribs and structure (his NOTES and PR #35), and the addition sheet he spot-checked is another code; Rosson's key is a second, independent ciphertext-only recovery.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 6174 tokens, 936 types, it-cinquecento order 4: reading -1.992 per letter; random keys -2.454 (z 14.0); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.081 (mean -2.097, z 8.9); annealer on the real text -2.073. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): per letter, Biermann's transcription and George Lasry's working decryption split verbatim out of lasry/transcription.json and lasry/decode.txt into texts/ (his files also linked), the project's own transcriptions of letters 1-3 (n20/), his excerpt translations, his key lasry/key.tsv; Rosson's independent reading linked to his page (his files are not in the repository).

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): texts/lasry_decode_letter4.txt read: the opening and closing build Italian sentences, but the middle has runs of open codes in most sentences. Per-document C confirmed; letter 4 relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part kept; fraction_read 0.929 -> 0.717.

Re-reading (batch b33): looked for images of BnF fr. 4050 ff. 79-81: the BnF Archives et manuscrits notice (free-text search 'Ranzo') shows fr. 4050 tome I item 30 with no Gallica digitisation; Gallica SRU blocked to scripts. No image reachable.

Paolo Rosson's public key (pangoleen/cipher-readings, centurione-1528, built on letters 1-3) applied to letter 4's open codes and tentative values: 3 of 90 open code types valued (e173 express, s72 sara, d46 debia), 9 of Lasry's tentative values confirmed.

The code list is numbered in rough alphabetical order within each initial, with neighbouring numbers often homophones; used with the sentence to propose values for 39 single-occurrence codes of letter 4 (e173 'express' reached before Rosson's key confirmed it). Values flagged sense-only in texts/letter4_reread_log.md; 47 code types left open.

Letter 4 joined into words by hand (texts/letter4_reading.md, English letter4_en.md; groups annotated by research/reading_audit/b33_rz_annot.py): body 0.768 clean sentences counting explicit holes, 0.404 plain against a modern Italian word list; one passage of eleven codes does not build. Decoded, not read -> read (B).

Verify sweep (reading audit v2): letter 4 (fr. 4050) re-scored with every [?word] counted as a hole (research/reading_audit/v2_score.py: the 39 sense-and-position code values, Lasry's tentative values seen once or twice, open codes): 0.591 (55/93) explicit holes, 0.376 plain, against 0.768 from b17 HOLES=1, which lets [?word] through as a known word; with only the 39 sense-only values as holes 0.776. Under the bar with the brief's rule ([?word] = partly carried = hole), and the eleven-code run 79r:27-79v:2 does not build. Demoted to decoded, not read; fraction_read back to 0.717.
Read bar applied per document (v10): 3 of 5 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.991; polyphony 0.0; 254 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.073

outcome.method_basis: George Lasry rebuilt his key from the ciphertext of Biermann's five-letter transcription with Italian cribs, repeated contexts and code-family structure (lasry/NOTES.md; PR #35); no decipherment, clear copy or key of these letters exists, and the 'Aditione nel zifra' he spot-checked is another code (1 of its 113 groups occurs here), so no external or adjacent plaintext supplied values. Paolo Rosson rebuilt a second key the same way, independently, on this project's transcription (6 Oct 2026); it agrees with Lasry's on 94-96% of the tokens both value, including letters 4 and 5, which Rosson never saw. This project's own annealer recovered only function words; its share is the transcription and the measurement.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Re-reading, 23 Oct 2026: letter 4 (fr. 4050) now reads, so the five letters that read are counted with their bar-measure read tokens: fr. 2988 f. 2 96.2% of 818, ff. 9-10 97.0% of 1,781, fr. 3022 no. 20 94.4% of 1,314, fr. 4050 87.7% of 1,559, fr. 6638 89.0% of 956 = 5,974 of 6,428 = 0.929 (the 22 Oct figure 0.717 left letter 4 out). 23 Oct 2026, verify sweep v2: letter 4 (fr. 4050) back to decoded, not read (0.591 with every [?word] counted as a hole), so it leaves the count again: 5,974 - 1,367 (87.7% of 1,559) = 4,607 of 6,428 = 0.717.

texts.label: Letter 1: Hieronimo Ranzo, BnF fr. 2988 ff. 2r-v (duplicate fr. 3019 ff. 73r-74r), Madrid, 27 March 1528
texts.summary: A letter signed by Hieronimo Ranzo, Gattinara's man, from Madrid in March 1528, in Ranzo's initial-letter code. Decryption: George Lasry's working decipherment (with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra) on Norbert Biermann's transcription; Paolo Rosson's independent reading, from its fr. 3019 duplicate, is on his own page (linked).
texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 93.7% of the words of texts/letter1_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.

texts.label: Letter 2: Hieronimo Ranzo, BnF fr. 2988 ff. 9r-10v (DECODE R1894), Madrid, March 1528
texts.summary: Ranzo's signed letter from Madrid, March 1528: instructions for writing to him through Hieronimo Ranzo, the 'zifra grande nostro' and payments by the army. Lasry's excerpt (f. 9v, translated in lasry/excerpts.json) describes a new compact cipher, sent with Cataneo, for letters that might be inspected overland.

texts.label: Letter 2, parallel copy: BnF fr. 20506 ff. 136-138 (DECODE R4450)
texts.summary: The parallel copy of letter 2 (fr. 2988 ff. 9-10). Biermann's transcription follows fr. 2988's line layout; there is no separate transcription of the copy, and its own variants are not checked against the images.
texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 93.3% of the words of texts/letter2_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.

texts.label: Letter 3: [Hieronimo Ranzo] to 'Garbino', BnF fr. 3022 no. 20, ff. 44r-46v, Madrid, 11 April 1528
texts.summary: An Italian letter, partly in clear, written from Madrid on 11 April 1528 to 'Garbino' (endorsement, f. 47v), almost certainly by Hieronimo Ranzo; Garbino's espionage kit (jargon sheet, code-name list, 'Aditione nel zifra') follows it in the volume. Lasry's decipherment and Rosson's independent reading (his page, linked) both cover it.
texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 92.0% of the words of texts/letter3_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.

texts.label: Letter 4: BnF fr. 4050 ff. 79-81
texts.summary: Hieronimo Ranzo, Madrid, 10 March 1528, to his agent: Cavalier Bilia's commission to inform the Duke (of Milan) through Ranzo; the declarations of war; Charles V's offer to the League envoys at Poza to restore the Duke, which they refused; advice to keep to the safer side; ships armed in Biscay seize 46 French vessels off Bordeaux; the Doña Guiomar money business and messer Iacomo; news to Garbino; a cipher addition sent.
texts.note: Verify sweep 23 Oct 2026 (reading audit v2): back to decoded, not read. The b33 reading (texts/letter4_reading.md, kept as a partial reading) scored 0.768 on explicit holes, but b17's HOLES=1 does not count a bracketed [?word] as a hole. With every [?word] counted (the 39 code values resting on sense and list position only, and Lasry's tentative values seen once or twice that Rosson's key does not confirm) and the open codes [a203] as holes, the body scores 0.591 (55/93; 0.376 plain), under the bar; counting only the 39 sense-only values gives 0.776. The passage 79r:27-79v:2 (eleven codes) does not build and 80r:1-3, 13-15 hold only in part. No image to check against: fr. 4050 is not digitised. Blockers: no-key-material (single-context codes), needs-physical-access (image of fr. 4050).

texts.label: Letter 5: BnF fr. 6638 pp. 67-70
texts.summary: Letter 5 of Lasry's edition, undated in his files and not seen by this project. Lasry's excerpt from p. 69 (translated in lasry/excerpts.json) gives the recipe for alum water for secret writing.
